wiki.title: Summit Linux Wiki
wiki.lead: Community documentation for Summit Linux and the picu package manager: concepts, commands, repositories and answers.
wiki.whatText: Summit Linux is an independent Linux distribution built from source following Linux From Scratch principles: transparent components, controlled builds and minimal software.
wiki.philoText: transparency instead of magic, a recipe instead of a black box.
wiki.installNote: This section is in developing — coming soon.
wiki.quickText: Daily workflow in three commands: sync indexes, install a package, upgrade the system.
wiki.cmdText: picu manages repositories, build recipes, binary packages, signatures, trust stores and the package database.
wiki.cmdSync: — fetch repository indexes and verify signatures.
wiki.cmdAdd: — install a package from a trusted mirror.
wiki.cmdCook: — build a package from source in isolation.
wiki.cmdCut: — remove a package and clean up untracked leftovers.
wiki.cmdInfo: — show version, recipe and mirror details.
wiki.cmdUpdate: — upgrade installed packages to the latest trusted versions.
wiki.cmdRebase: — rebuild a local recipe against the current base.
wiki.cmdTrust: — show trusted keys and revoked certificates.
wiki.mirrorsNoteText: they require explicit trust — never enable an untrusted mirror with unsafe flags on a production system.
wiki.faq1q: Is Summit Linux ready for daily use?
wiki.faq1a: The project is a working concept with a staged implementation plan; follow the News page for releases.
wiki.faq2q: How is picu different from other package managers?
wiki.faq2a: picu combines source recipes and binary packages with cryptographic verification of every repository index.
wiki.faq3q: Which init system does Summit use?
wiki.faq3a: OpenRC / sysvinit with an optional runit setup.
wiki.faq4a: Releases will be checksummed and repository indexes will be signed; see the Download page for details.
wiki.faq5q: Can I build packages from source?
wiki.faq5a: Yes — use picu cook with a recipe file for an isolated, reproducible build.
wiki.faq6a: In the Markdown-files-and-info repository and on the Download page.
wiki.faq7q: Which picu commands will I use most?
wiki.faq7a: picu sync, picu add, picu update, picu find and picu info for daily work; picu cook and picu cut for source builds; picu trust for key management.
wiki.faq8q: How do I add a community mirror?
wiki.faq8a: Add its description to /etc/picu/mirrors.d/ and grant it explicit trust — community mirrors are never trusted by default.
wiki.faq9q: What if a signature check fails?
wiki.faq9a: Do not install anything: re-run picu sync, check the index expiry date and your trusted keys, then report the mirror.

abt.baseP: Summit is aimed at experienced Linux users and follows an LFS/source-build model.
abt.feat.1: Source-first: LFS-based toolchain with declarative build recipes.
abt.feat.2: Minimal base: CLI-only default install, no hidden services.
abt.feat.3: Your init, your choice: OpenRC / sysvinit with optional runit.
abt.feat.4: Reproducible builds: fixed flags, isolated build environment, checksummed sources.
abt.feat.5: Signed everything: repository indexes, releases and recipes are cryptographically verified.
abt.feat.6: Downgrade protection: version checks and expiry dates on repository metadata.
abt.goalText: a minimal, auditable base you can rebuild from scratch on any machine.
abt.intro: Summit Linux is an independent Linux distribution built from source following Linux From Scratch principles.
abt.missionP: Give experienced users a system they can fully explain: every binary traces back to a readable recipe, every repository index carries a verifiable signature, and nothing is installed that the user did not ask for.
abt.philoText: transparency instead of magic, a recipe instead of a black box.
abt.stackP: picu is written in Rust and combines source recipes with binary packages: it fetches signed indexes, resolves dependencies, builds in isolation with picu cook, and installs transactionally into a tracked file registry.
abt.styleP: Summit uses a cool snow-inspired palette based on blue, white and light gray.
